limits.statement: The behavior-tested level never certifies. In certification-behavior-all-eligible-still-blocked the persistence hand-off and the runtime projection are both reported eligible and every required evidence kind is present, and the result is still blocked with behavior-handoff-not-integrated as its only blocker and certifiedLevel null, because evaluateCompositionCertification appends that blocker whenever the requested level is behavior-tested. Every input of that fixture is synthetic: the persistence hand-off, the runtime binding, the evidence pair, both execution-evidence documents and the projection are assembled by the fixture language from constants (repeated-character hashes, a fixed attempt nonce, a fixed revision, the profile legacy-http-fixture/1), and no run of the persistence track (T10) or of the evaluation track (T16) produced them. Promotion of behavior-tested needs verifier-produced hand-offs that were accepted for the exact revision, profile and combination, and a certification module that no longer appends the blocker; this record has neither and claims neither.

Only the combinations that listApprovedCombinations returns are supported: java-spring with jpa-hibernate, python-fastapi with sqlalchemy-sqlmodel and typescript-express with typeorm, each with a uuid key and the status legacy-provider. For any other provider, persistence layer or key type (also when one of the three is not given) resolveApprovedCombination returns null; previewGeneration then returns the short blocked plan before the provider emit is called (status blocked, combination null, blocker unsupported-combination, and no resourceDecisions, manualCompletions or forcedWrites field); evaluateCompositionCertification adds the blocker unsupported-combination; describeResourceGeneration throws for a provider without a conservative profile. A persistence layer or key type that was not given is printed as undefined in the blocker message.

Every plan and every certification result carries applyAllowed false, also when the plan is ready and when the certification is certified. previewGeneration calls the provider emit with dryRun true, computeDiff false and force false (plan-java-ready-with-emit-arguments-echo shows the arguments a stub emit received), and evaluateCompositionCertification blocks a preview whose applyAllowed is not false (unsafe-preview-contract). The six modules contain no path that applies, writes or forces a generation; a ready plan and a certified result describe a dry run. What a real provider emit does when it is called with dryRun true is not replayed here (see real-provider-emit-is-not-replayed).

The behavior-tested inputs persistenceHandoff and runtimeBehavior are spread after the expectation that evaluateCompositionCertification builds from the approved combination, the revision and the profile, so an object that the caller passes under the key expected replaces the expectation of the layer. A hand-off made for the java tuple is refused for the python request (certification-forged-handoff-for-other-tuple-rejected, handoff-combination-mismatch) but becomes eligible when the same input carries an expected object of its own (certification-caller-expected-replaces-the-layer-expectation); a runtime projection for another combination and profile behaves the same way (the two runtime fixtures). The result still ends blocked, only because of behavior-handoff-not-integrated. This is the behaviour at the base commit, recorded as an observed defect and not changed here; binding a hand-off to the requested combination is not supported when the caller supplies expected.

describeResourceGeneration grants generation from one flag: willGenerateResolver must be the boolean true. An explicit non-UUID key (idFieldIsUuid false) adds a reason but does not stop a resource that the provider plan approved (safety-non-uuid-key-still-generated); a null entry in the resource list is skipped with a null resource type instead of being rejected; a missing handles plan yields no decisions and no error; a requested resource that is absent is reported in requestedMissing only. python-fastapi and typescript-express generate fail-closed authorization and patch stubs and list manual completions for them, so authorization and patch semantics are not wired by this layer; java-spring leaves authorization, patch and recover to the provider policy and lists no manual completion. The profile is a lookup table of stub names; nothing here evaluates whether generated code is safe.

describeResourceGeneration and requiredEvidenceFor read the provider profile and the build evidence kind with a plain property read on an object literal, so an inherited name of Object.prototype passes as a provider id (the fixtures use constructor). describeResourceGeneration then does not throw: the decision of a generated resource carries undefined fetch, authorization, patch and recover columns and no manual completion is listed (safety-inherited-provider-name-accepted). requiredEvidenceFor at the build level returns a function as its third evidence kind (required-evidence-inherited-provider-name-listed), and evaluateCompositionCertification reports a missing-evidence blocker whose kind is that function and whose message holds the function source text (certification-inherited-provider-name-missing-evidence-kind-is-a-function). previewGeneration is not affected, because resolveApprovedCombination compares the provider id with strict equality and answers unsupported-combination before the safety profile is read. This is the behaviour at the base commit, recorded as an observed defect and not changed here; an own-property lookup of provider ids is not supported.

inspectRuntimeBehaviorProjection compares the values of the runtime binding, the evidence pair, the two evidence documents and the projection with each other and checks the format of one value only: candidate_hash must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, else candidate-artifact-unbound. An empty run_id, an empty attempt_nonce, a malformed case_revision_hash, an empty oracle_profile_approval_hash, a null contract_hash, a null flow_hash and an artifacts value of any type leave the result eligible when the other documents repeat the same value (evidence-runtime-empty-identity-values-eligible). The two hashes of the evidence pair are compared with the evidence documents only when they are truthy: an empty string or null skips the comparison and the result stays eligible (evidence-runtime-empty-pair-hashes-not-compared), while a non-empty wrong hash is refused with oracle-evidence-hash-mismatch (evidence-runtime-wrong-pair-hash-refused). The attempt_nonce of the evidence pair is not compared with the one of the binding when the binding one is empty: an empty binding attempt_nonce, an empty projection attemptNonce and a pair that names another attempt_nonce, with every hash recomputed, leave the result eligible (evidence-runtime-empty-binding-nonce-pair-nonce-not-compared). Equality is all this layer proves about those fields; whether they are meaningful is not decided here.

The legacy provider audit, the plan and the certification carry the schema ids sbf.handles-provider-baseline-audit/0, sbf.handles-composition-plan/0 and sbf.handles-composition-certification/0, and the bound-evidence check expects the internal evidence id bskel.internal.handles-composition-evidence/0, which the module itself describes as not a stable schema. All of them are version 0: the vocabulary is not a frozen cross-track interface, and no file outside the layer names these ids (see layer-is-not-consumed-outside-its-directories), so no schema file or consumer pins them. Nothing recorded here is a stable capability or a promotion claim.

The root test script is node --test test/*.test.mjs, which matches test files directly under test/ and not test/provider-composition-next. The suite runs through node scripts/run-next-nested-tests.mjs T14 (the CI job nested-next) or through node --test on its test files (the direct-tap command), so a green root npm test is not T14 evidence. The package test test/package-install.test.mjs packs and installs the package, whose files list includes handles/; it does not run this suite either.

requiredEvidenceFor does not look at the provider at the preview level: an unknown provider gets the same evidence kinds as a known one (composition-unit and package-install), and only the build and behavior levels throw for a provider without a build evidence profile. A preview-tested certification request for an unlisted provider is therefore blocked by unsupported-combination plus one missing-evidence blocker per kind, not by one statement that the provider is unknown. At the build level the same missing profile is reported with the code unsupported-certification-level, which also names an unknown level. Whether preview evidence for an unlisted provider would mean anything is not decided here.

auditLegacyProviders compares only the providers whose id is one of expectedProviderIds (java-spring, python-fastapi, typescript-express): a provider with another id in the list is not inspected and the audit stays ok; a missing provider is an error; a null list is tolerated like an empty one. For each of the three it compares the contract id, the capability list, outputs.spec and whether plan and emit are functions with constants held in legacy-baseline.mjs. It does not call the providers and does not look at what they generate. A provider without an outputs object is reported as outputs.spec changed to [undefined] and its observed outputsSpec is undefined. A passing audit says that the registry shape of the three providers is unchanged, not that their generation is correct.

At the preview-tested and build-tested levels evaluateCompositionCertification accepts plain objects: the baseline audit needs ok true and the same revision, the generation preview needs status ready, the same revision, applyAllowed false, the provider id and the combination id, and an evidence record needs kind, revision, status success and a scope with the provider id and the combination id (source, runId and artifactRef are copied when present and are otherwise null). In certification-preview-tested-certified-from-minimal-objects a hand-written audit, a hand-written preview and plain records give the status certified. validateBoundCertificationEvidence, which checks canonical evidence bytes against an artifact reference of six keys, is a separate export that certification.mjs does not call (it imports only inspectPersistenceHandoff and inspectRuntimeBehaviorProjection from evidence-boundary.mjs; interface-rfc.test.mjs checks the import list); given a plain object instead of bytes it refuses (evidence-bound-plain-object-rejected), and given matching canonical bytes it accepts (evidence-bound-accepted). A certified preview-tested or build-tested result therefore states that records were presented, not that evidence was produced, bound to bytes or verified.

previewGeneration trusts what the provider and the handles plan hand it. An emit that returns nothing leaves the plan ready with no planned writes and no blockers; written, forced, notes and postEmitNotes keep their string entries and silently drop the others; an action that is not an object becomes an entry with null path, kind and action; conflicts, orphans and registrationGaps that are not arrays are ignored; an entry without text gets a default message and a missing path becomes null; a handles plan that names no provider is accepted for any provider; an empty resourceFilter selects no resource instead of all. None of this is rejected. The plan status follows from the pre-emit checks and from the three blocker lists that emit reports.

No file outside handles/composition-next and test/provider-composition-next names an export of the layer (t16HashJson aside, see hash-rule-has-a-second-copy) or one of its schema ids at the base commit: the absence pattern matches no file, while the control pattern composition-next still finds the files listed under control (the CI workflow, the ownership map, one RFC of another track and the nested runner), so the search itself works. By this search nothing else in the repository imports or calls the layer, and no plan or certification it produces is consumed anywhere. A call with a computed path or a re-export under another name would not match.

The files listed under references name T14 at the base commit (recomputed with git grep): the CI workflow step, the ownership map and the write-scope fixture, the nested runner, the project-graph RFC row that lists handles/composition-next/** with owner T14, and documents, code and tests of the persistence track (scanners/persistence-next, test/persistence-next). That track states that its hand-off uses the provider, persistence and key vocabulary of this catalog, that this catalog stays the final fail-closed allowlist, and that its hand-off status bound proves identity only and independent acceptance is still required. Those are statements of that track; this record does not verify them, and it records no run in which a persistence-next hand-off reached this layer.

inspectRuntimeBehaviorProjection requires a runtime binding (beval.runtime-binding/1), an evidence pair (beval.runtime-evidence-pair/1) and two execution-evidence documents that carry the contract id beval.execution-evidence/1. The binding id appears outside the layer in the files listed under control, but no file outside the layer contains the string beval.execution-evidence/1 (the absence pattern matches nothing); the shorter word execution-evidence appears outside the layer only in the file listed under references. So the repository holds no producer and no schema for the execution-evidence document that this layer demands, and the fixtures build such a document themselves. This is a search result at the base commit, not a proof that no producer exists: an id built at run time would not match.

inspectPersistenceHandoff wants a provenance record whose status is accepted and inspectRuntimeBehaviorProjection wants a projection whose producerApproval is accepted (evidence-handoff-eligible and evidence-runtime-eligible show inputs that are eligible; evidence-handoff-bound-provenance-refused shows that a provenance with the status bound is refused with handoff-not-approved). No file outside handles/composition-next and test/provider-composition-next sets either word as a value at the base commit: the absence pattern matches no file, while the control pattern finds the persistence-next binder, whose own note says that independent acceptance is still required and whose provenance status is bound, not accepted. Whether an acceptance step will exist, who will own it and what it will emit is unknown; this layer cannot be shown to work against a real producer (see packed-artifact-and-real-t10-t16-input).

control.pattern: independent T19/T14 acceptance is still required

limits.statement: evidence-boundary.mjs implements the hash of a JSON value (sha256 of the key-sorted, two-space-indented text with a final newline) as t16HashJson and describes it as an independent consumer implementation of the rule of the evaluation track. The files listed under references, outside the layer, contain another function of the same name (the reconciliation track and its tests). No fixture compares the two copies, so their agreement is not recorded; evidence-t16-hash-of-known-value pins the digest that this copy gives for one value with unsorted keys.

Three fixtures record the message of a TypeError that the JavaScript engine raised, not the layer (certification-null-evidence-throws, certification-without-argument-throws and evidence-runtime-non-array-exchanges-throws). The texts were identical on Node 22 and Node 24, the two majors the record was run on, but they belong to V8: another engine version may word them differently and the replay of those three fixtures would then fail without any change in the layer.

The fixtures of this record and the existing tests of the suite drive previewGeneration only with stub providers, whose emit returns fixed values or echoes the arguments it received. The three real provider modules are audited (id, contract, requiresCapabilities, outputs.spec, plan and emit are functions) and two real resolver templates are read by an existing test for their fail-closed labels, but no real emit function is called. What a real emit returns when it is called with dryRun true is not recorded.

The layer is run from a checkout (an extracted copy of the base commit). It is not run from a packed or installed npm package although the package files list includes handles/, and no real persistence-track hand-off and no runtime evidence from a real evaluation run is fed to it. A packed-artifact result and an integrated cross-track input are not recorded and not claimed here.

The pinned files reach ajv and ajv-formats through lib/schema-validate.mjs, which the provider modules and the engine import. The commands run in an extracted copy of the base commit whose node_modules is linked to the node_modules of the checkout that runs them (installed by npm ci). Before the link is made, the version of every package the pinned files import, and of the packages those require, is compared with the version that the pinned package-lock.json states (environment.loaded_packages), and a difference fails the test. The scan of the imports is textual, so a specifier built at run time is not seen, and the files inside the installed packages are not hashed: only their versions are compared.

Only minimal hand-written inputs are recorded: stub providers, small handles plans, plain evidence records and evidence documents that the fixture language builds from constants. Behaviour on real application scans, real provider output or real CI evidence, and any performance or scale figure, is not recorded.

The recorded outputs, hashes and counts were generated on one machine (macOS arm64) with one Node major; the replays were also run with a second Node major, but other operating systems and architectures were not observed.

verification.recomputed: bytes, git_blob_sha1 and sha256 of every pinned file, per-file and total test counts, the exit code and counts of both commands, the first runner line, every fixture output hash and every expected value, the reference lists of the limits that carry them (the files that match a pattern, and the empty list of an absence claim together with the positive control that shows the search can find something), the installed version of every package in environment.loaded_packages against package-lock.json at the base commit, and the per-file table, every test count, the NESTED_SUITE line and the base commit that INTERFACE_RFC.md states are compared by baseline-record.test.mjs with the values it recomputed, never with a copy kept in the document.
levels: always: the record is well formed, and any single tampered hash, size, test count, exit code, expected value, limit status or commit id is reported; artifact_digest covers every field except its own value, so an edit of a limit statement, a fixture class, a call, a title or this text that is not re-sealed is reported

live files: size, sha256 and blob id are recomputed from the checkout; a file that disagrees in one hash or in size alone is damage and fails; a file that matches neither hash is drift, which skips the live replays while the pinned commit decides

pinned commit: the base commit is fetched once when absent and the sizes and digests of all pinned files, the runner included, are recomputed from its own blobs; if the commit is unavailable the test fails, and only BASELINE_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=1 turns that into an explicit skip
ancestry: a shallow checkout is deepened with git fetch --no-tags --unshallow origin and the base commit must be an ancestor of HEAD

commands: both recorded commands are re-run in an extracted copy of the base commit (node_modules linked from the checkout once the installed versions equal environment.loaded_packages, which package-lock.json at the base commit states) and must reproduce exit code, counts, per-file counts and every fixture output

references: the files outside the track directories that match each recorded pattern are recomputed with git grep at the pinned commit and must equal the list in the limit; a limit that claims absence must match no file with its pattern while its control pattern still finds the listed files

documents: the per-file table, every "<n> tests" figure, the NESTED_SUITE line and the base commit in INTERFACE_RFC.md describe the pinned base commit and are compared with this record, whose counts and first runner line the commands level reproduces; interface-rfc.test.mjs compares the vocabulary of the RFC with the code
not_recomputed: ci_observations: read once from the CI API (gh api, read-only) and kept for traceability; no test re-reads them
environment: describes the machine this record was generated on

prose: limit statements, fixture origins, the title and this text are bound only by artifact_digest, which reports an edit that is not re-sealed; an editor who re-seals the record is caught only by review of the diff and by the recomputed values above
the files inside the installed packages (ajv, ajv-formats and the packages they require): not hashed; only their versions are compared with package-lock.json at the base commit

support data: the persistence hand-off, the runtime binding, the evidence pair and the execution evidence in the fixtures are synthetic documents that the fixture language assembles from constants (repeated-character hashes, a fixed attempt nonce, fixed revisions); no run of persistence-next or beval produced them and their values are not independently checked
INTERFACE_RFC.md: only the numbers and the base commit named above are recomputed here, and its vocabulary by interface-rfc.test.mjs, not the explanatory text
